title: Executive at IT Reseller Sees DocuSign Revenue Growing 12%–13% Across Accounts in 2026 Despite Pricing Pressure
expert: Account executive at a national IT reseller managing seven mid-enterprise accounts; Docusign ~60% of his category revenue
verdict: A recent renewal grew roughly 10% on ~10% higher envelope usage, and IAM package prices rose 10%–20% with a 5%–10% early-adopter discount ended, though one customer is building an in-house API alternative.

Back to double-digit growth: 🟢 **Renewal up roughly 10%** on ~10% envelope growth, in line with +~10.2% on the 2026-11-09 VAR AE call.
🟢 **12%–13% across his accounts in CY26** (estimate) vs ~10% on the 2026-11-09 call.
IAM adoption: 🟢 **IAM package prices up 10%–20%**, early-adopter discount of 5%–10% ended after 2026-01-31; matches ~20% on the 2026-11-05 consulting PMO call.
DBNR / renewal expansion: 🟡 **Seats up around 10%–12%** (estimate), consistent with +~11% on 2026-11-09 but vs -5%–7% on 2026-11-06 (PSA-software COO).
🔴 **One customer building an in-house API alternative** at a fraction of the price to avoid per-envelope fees.

changes: Renewal +~10% and CY26 12%–13% (estimate) vs +~10.2% and ~10% CY26 (2026-11-09, VAR AE): consistent.
IAM package price +10%–20% vs ~20% IAM increase (2026-11-05, consulting PMO) and Cleveland ~5-10% ACV uplift (SB #63574): consistent.
Seats +10%–12% vs +~11% (2026-11-09, VAR AE): consistent; vs -5%–7% (2026-11-06, PSA-software COO): conflicting.
thesis_impact: Stance (neutral; DD growth): ↑ — 12%–13% expected across his accounts for CY26 (estimate).
Stance (IAM bet): ↑ — IAM pricing up 10%–20% and discounts withdrawn without lost renewals.
